parent_section_or_group: Part 2B — Notification of cyber security incidents
source_access_notes: Official compilation C2026C00213 primary HTML; provision context, Application Rules r5 and Definitions Rules r18 reviewed. No operational portal fields inferred.
governance_expectation: When the complete statutory critical incident trigger is satisfied for a covered asset and its responsible entity, give ASD an incident report including information prescribed by the rules, as soon as practicable and in any event within 12 hours after the entity becomes so aware. The initial report may be oral or written; if written, use the approved form.

interpretation_provenance.source_analysis_method: Primary-text clause review preserves governed actor, compound conditional duty, awareness and oral-report clocks, recipient, form, exceptions and applicability dependencies. Maintainer approved the concrete package; no human source verification claimed.

review_limitations: Only the bounded reporting proposition is represented. Operational approved-form fields and whole-Act completeness are not claimed.
requirement_summary: When the complete statutory critical incident trigger is satisfied for a covered asset and its responsible entity, give ASD an incident report including information prescribed by the rules, as soon as practicable and in any event within 12 hours after the entity becomes so aware. The initial report may be oral or written; if written, use the approved form.
applicable_actor: Responsible entity for an asset to which Part 2B applies, as defined by the actual asset class and s12L
timing_or_frequency: As soon as practicable and in any event within 12 hours after the specified awareness trigger.
required_artefacts: Incident report, with information (if any) prescribed by rules; approved form if submitted in writing.
applicability_conditions: Part 2B must apply to the asset under s30BB: the applicable rules or a s51 declaration, subject to any s30BB(3) / Application Rules r5(5) grace period.
The asset and responsible entity must satisfy ss9 and 12L and the applicable class definitions/rules. Sectors under s8D are not automatically Part 2B asset coverage.
Apply the constitutional/entity scope in s13 and the extraterritorial provision in s14 together with s9(2B) outside-Australia asset limitation and ss9(2C)-(2D) satellite/submarine-cable exceptions.
Use cyber security incident in s12M and unauthorised access/modification/impairment in s12N, including the actual entitlement, employee/agent scope and authorised-law-enforcement qualifications.

Report recipient is ASD under s30BF read with Definitions Rules r18. The Department is specified only for ss30BC(5) and 30BD(5) written-record exemption powers; it is not substituted as the ordinary report recipient.
The responsible entity becomes aware that a cyber security incident has occurred or is occurring.
The entity becomes aware that the incident has had or is having a significant direct or indirect impact on asset availability.

Significant impact is the if-and-only-if test in s30BEA: material disruption of essential goods/services supplied using the asset, or circumstances specified in rules. Imminence alone is not this trigger.
exceptions_or_qualifications: The written-record exemption under subsection (5) concerns the oral-report follow-up duty under subsection (3), not the initial notification duty.
s30BE supplies specified good-faith damages protections; this is not a general immunity from reporting duties or every form of liability.
constituent_propositions: Give the incident report to the statutory recipient.
Include information, if any, prescribed by rules.
Meet both as-soon-as-practicable and outer-limit timing.
Where the initial report is written, use the approved form.

governance_expectation: If the responsible entity gives an oral report under s30BD(1), make a written record in the approved form and give a copy to ASD within 48 hours after that oral report, unless the entity has a written exemption under s30BD(5) for that incident.

requirement_summary: If the responsible entity gives an oral report under s30BD(1), make a written record in the approved form and give a copy to ASD within 48 hours after that oral report, unless the entity has a written exemption under s30BD(5) for that incident.
applicable_actor: Responsible entity for an asset to which Part 2B applies, as defined by the actual asset class and s12L
governed_object: Approved-form written record and delivery of a previously oral statutory incident report
timing_or_frequency: Within 48 hours after the oral report is given; this clock does not run from initial incident awareness.
required_artefacts: Written record in the approved form and a copy given to ASD.
applicability_conditions: Part 2B must apply to the asset under s30BB: the applicable rules or a s51 declaration, subject to any s30BB(3) / Application Rules r5(5) grace period.
The asset and responsible entity must satisfy ss9 and 12L and the applicable class definitions/rules. Sectors under s8D are not automatically Part 2B asset coverage.

Use cyber security incident in s12M and unauthorised access/modification/impairment in s12N, including the actual entitlement, employee/agent scope and authorised-law-enforcement qualifications.

Report recipient is ASD under s30BF read with Definitions Rules r18. The Department is specified only for ss30BC(5) and 30BD(5) written-record exemption powers; it is not substituted as the ordinary report recipient.
The responsible entity becomes aware that a cyber security incident has occurred, is occurring or is imminent.
The entity becomes aware that the incident has had, is having or is likely to have a relevant impact on the asset.
Relevant impact is defined by s8G, including direct/indirect availability, integrity, reliability and specified confidentiality effects.
The heading other does not erase a concurrently triggered critical reporting duty or extend its 12-hour clock.
An oral initial report was actually given under s30BD(1).
exceptions_or_qualifications: The written-record exemption under subsection (5) concerns the oral-report follow-up duty under subsection (3), not the initial notification duty.
s30BE supplies specified good-faith damages protections; this is not a general immunity from reporting duties or every form of liability.
Definitions Rules r18 specifies the Department for s30BD(5); preserve written-notice scope, delegation and direction conditions in s30BD(5)-(8).
constituent_propositions: Make a written record of the oral report in the approved form.
Give a copy to the statutory recipient within the distinct follow-up period.
